analysis:
This PR is documentation only: docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md, docs/architecture/telemetry.md and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. No executable code changed, so I found no concrete regression. It documents Swift-side behavior (adoption, placement holds, busy reasons, transition watchdog) that was not supplied, so I cannot verify the implementation matches the text.

Things the next pass should check against the Swift source:
1. Adoption (model-autopilot.md lines 40-51) lets a succeeded operation's cached-inventory target keep serving without a lease. This is relevant to T-052, T-053 and TB-011. The docs say adoption ends on consent revoke, deselect, residency loss, failed self-test, unverifiable weight hash or shutdown, and grants serving only. Confirm in ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift that `autopilotServesModel` does not bypass the ordinary weight-hash and verified-build gates (T-012, T-027), and that `reconcileAutopilotPlacements` runs on every end condition.
2. `hold_seconds` (protocol-messages.md, around line 1208) is bounded to 0...86400 and rejected as `invalid_command` without `load_model_id`. Holds could pin memory and cause denial of service, but the docs state they are per-model, expire, skip LRU and idle unload, and never affect other models. Confirm the 86400 bound is enforced in code. Holds are honored only for providers reporting `placement_holds`.
3. The new heartbeat and status fields (`busy_reasons`, `busy_reason`, `busy_since_ms`, `transition_stalls`, `capabilities`, `adopted_models`, `held_models`, `detail`) are consent-gated. The vocabularies are closed enums and contain no prompt content, which fits the telemetry policy and A-001. They expose coarse provider residency and activity metadata to the coordinator, which is already trusted.
4. The watchdog (model-autopilot.md lines 65-82) cancels only a stalled operation. A preload stall answers `failed` while the load may still complete, and the docs describe that explicitly. Confirm in the code that the fences are not cleared (T-010).
5. protocol-messages.md cites an immutable platform commit for tolerance of unknown keys. Older coordinator behavior was not independently verified.

The threat model has no Autopilot-specific threat for adoption or holds. A future update could add one, but this is not a regression.
